I intend to announce new restrictions on foreign travel and shipping which will greatly reduce the chance of incidents with Germany, and thus reestablish a true neutrality in this war.
I am proud to have kept this country out of war, and I will make every effort to do so if elected for a second term.
I don't intend to explicitly rebuke such claims, but I will not emphasize the peace issue as I campaign this fall.
I pray for peace, but we will not compromise the rights of American shipping and commerce. We are fully prepared to take the fight to Germany if interference continues.
A vote for Mr. Hughes is a vote for war. He was an admirable Justice, but he is sympathy with the most bellicose elements of the Republican Party.
I don't plan to say much about Charles Evans Hughes one way or the other. I believe we have better things to campaign on.
We have taken extensive efforts to increase the military preparedness of the United States. For Mr. Hughes and others to insinuate otherwise is simply false.
The pacifists in your party are revitalized by your acceptance speech.
Even for the anti-war sentiment of the times, this is a little too passive for many.
This is just what most Democrats want to hear.
You have plenty of other issues to campaign on, but most of your supporters are hoping to hear more on the peace issue.
You sound as bellicose as Teddy Roosevelt on this issue, to the great disappointment of many in your party.
What position will you take in regards to the war in Europe as you campaign?

Mr. Wilson's vacillations on the issue have emboldened potential adversaries and led to unfortunate events like the sinking of the Lusitania. A more resolute policy would actually increase the chances for peace.
As President, I have no desire for war. However, I will spare no effort to protect the legitimate rights of American shipping and commerce.
If Mr. Wilson continues to allow American ships to travel in dangerous areas, it is only a matter of time before we are drawn into war. His claims to be the peace candidate ring hollow.
Wilson has repeatedly taken half-measures, when we should be doing much more to prepare for the threat of war.
I refuse to politicize the security of the United States. Wilson and I are both in support of the current measures.
Preparedness is a bellicose policy which leads us closer to the very thing we are preparing against -- war, that is.
body: “他让我们置身战争之外”强调威尔逊此前任内没有使美国参战，是1916年民主党竞选的重要口号。不能把它自动改写成无论情况如何、永不参战的法律保证。
兰辛的回忆录记述了口号传播及共和党对中立政策的批评。游戏中的“投休斯就是投战争”是人物的可选攻击话术，这里不将它认证为某位候选人的逐字史实引语。

sources.title: 罗伯特·兰辛《战争回忆录》：1916年竞选章，第160—162页（公开转录）

notes.title: 工伤赔偿：联邦雇员与危险行业的范围差别
contains: Do you support the broader establishment of workers' compensation programs and laws, at the federal level?
I support a federal workers' compensation program which all dangerous industries would be required to participate in.
I do support the effort this year to establish workers' compensation for federal employees.
This is not a measure that I support.
body: 工伤赔偿针对因工作受伤或职业病等情形提供补偿，不是普遍加薪。1916年《联邦雇员赔偿法》扩展了联邦文职雇员的保护。
原作分别提供建立更广泛的危险行业制度、仅支持联邦雇员措施及反对的选项。它们的适用范围不同，不能在中文中合并成一句“支持工人福利”。

sources.title: 美国劳工部：1916年联邦雇员赔偿立法沿革

notes.title: 国际联盟：1916年仍是未来设想
contains: Would you support American participation in a postwar League of Nations, if one were to be created after the current War?
I support a League of Nations, and American participation in it. We can no longer safely ignore the affairs of the world.
I don't have any comment on this plan. It's far too early to determine how the war will end, who will win, or what the peace arrangements might be.
I support the traditional policy of non-interference in European affairs, as is best for our national interest.
The League of Nations idea is viewed with suspicion by many conservatives, and anti-war progressives alike.
There's nothing wrong with postponing judgment on this issue.
body: 1916年已有关于战后国际组织的倡议，但国际联盟正式开始活动是在1920年1月10日。游戏所说“若战后成立”，讨论的是未来设想，不是1916年已存在的组织。
反对干预欧洲、暂缓判断与支持未来组织，表达的是不同的外交立场；国际联盟也不能直接译成后来的联合国。

sources.title: 联合国日内瓦办事处：国际联盟设想与正式成立时间

notes.title: “责任到我这里为止”：不是一美元停在桌上
contains: I stand by my actions 100%. The buck stops here.
body: 杜鲁门桌上的名牌写着“The Buck Stops Here”，意为责任到此为止，不能再推给别人。这里的buck不是通常所说的一美元。
杜鲁门图书馆解释它与“推卸责任”的说法及扑克牌中轮到谁发牌的标记有关，同时对词源使用“据说”的措辞。游戏借这个政治口头禅表达承担责任，并非把所有可选发言都认证为历史上的原话。

sources.title: 杜鲁门总统图书馆：名牌原物、推责习语与词源说明

notes.title: “无所作为的国会”与“萝卜日”特别会期
contains: Is there anything you can say during your acceptance speech at the national convention to shake this race up?

You are calling for a pretty far-reaching platform as you campaign, but the current Congress has refused to consider many of your proposals. How will things be different in your next term if you are elected?

The Republicans are putting out a nice platform, but their own Congress has sandbagged half of these proposals in the past two years alone. I will call Congress into session and make them put their money where their mouth is.
When I get elected, we're going to get a Democratic Congress with me. That's how it's done.
I'm calling Congress into session now so that the American people can see how little they are capable of accomplishing. If they don't vote the Republicans out this fall then I don't know what to say.
People will definitely have second-thoughts when they see the Republican Congress turn its back on its own platform. Consensus seems to be that this was a brilliant maneuver on your part.
Way to remind the American people about the ineffectual Congress we have.

Your party has passed a fairly ambitious and liberal platform which you have supported. However, if the Republican Congress won't pass these laws now, how do you expect to push them forward as President?

Just in the past 12 months, Congress has passed the Marshall Plan and Taft-Hartley with bipartisan support. They have passed an expansive farm bill, and will be considering housing legislation soon. I don't see why I couldn't work with this Congress.
I believe that a Republican Congress, working with a Republican President, will be able to come to accord on the key issues of our time.
body: 杜鲁门在1948年接受提名演说中，宣布召集国会于7月26日开特别会期，要求共和党议员用实际行动兑现本党党纲。他称国会无所作为，是竞选攻击，并非字面上指国会没有通过任何法律。
“萝卜日”借用密苏里州夏季播种萝卜的俗语。原文put their money where their mouth is意为拿出行动兑现承诺，不是要求议员真的交钱。特别会期实际上通过了针对通胀和住房的两项法案。

sources.title: 美国参议院：“萝卜日”会期的演说、两项法案与竞选争论

notes.title: Whistle-stop：乘火车沿途停车演说
contains: You are making a whistle-stop tour of the country to promote your candidacy. What region will you visit over the next two weeks?
I will pledge to visit every state in the Union before election day. I stand for every working man in this country, and I'll let them know all about it before this is done.
We're going up the Eastern Seaboard, from Maryland all the way to Connecticut.
We're going to hit the Midwest, from Ohio to Wisconsin and Iowa.
I'm going through the Plains and Mountain states. I could personally talk to a third of the voters in that region, as sparsely populated as it is.
We're going to hit the West Coast, and especially California.
Everywhere you go, large crowds await you. Dewey seems to have the advantage in the polls, but pundits admire your spunk and your fiery speaking style.
There is some chatter about whether these crowds you're drawing signify anything. You're the underdog for sure, but maybe you're on to something.
We'll barnstorm as much of the Midwest as we can, going from state to state.
You're certainly drawing good crowds, but word has it that Truman is doing even better on that front. Fortunately you should win where it matters -- in the ballot box.
body: 这里指候选人乘火车旅行，沿途停车，在车厢后部平台向群众演说的竞选方式。不能译成吹哨举报，也不是停止吹口哨。
杜鲁门图书馆保存了1948年列车、站点和演说记录。游戏里夸口能亲自和当地三分之一选民交谈，是人物的竞选修辞，旁注不把这项比例当作实测史实。

sources.title: 杜鲁门总统图书馆：1948年竞选列车与巡回地图档案

notes.title: “杜威击败杜鲁门”：著名的错误头条
contains:
Congratulations! You have won the 1948 Presidential Election.

In a comeback for the ages, you defeated Thomas Dewey and shocked the nation. Prepare for another four years in the White House. There is much work to be done. You have an ambitious domestic agenda, and face a dangerous foreign situation with the Soviet Union. With a new Democratic majority in Congress, you can hopefully push for universal health care and a repeal of the Taft-Hartley Act.

Sorry. You have lost the 1948 Presidential Election.

Pundits and political pros are shocked at your collapse. The second-guessing will likely come fast and furious from your party. The Republicans have now lost five Presidential elections in a row, and have no obvious standard-bearer to break the trend in 1952. As for your own career, you are still the Governor of New York, but it is pretty unlikely that you'll be given another chance to prove yourself on the national stage.
Everywhere you go, large crowds await you. Dewey seems to have the advantage in the polls, but pundits admire your spunk and your fiery speaking style.
There is some chatter about whether these crowds you're drawing signify anything. You're the underdog for sure, but maybe you're on to something.
Let's see if you've managed to pull it off. Election night will be interesting.
Another attack on Truman. Political junkies are delighted by the back-and-forth in this campaign between the two of you.
Advisers like the bland, non-committal nature of this answer. The important thing is to play it safe and preserve your lead in the polls.
What an exciting last day of the campaign! Let's see how the voting goes tomorrow.
body: 1948年《芝加哥论坛报》曾刊出“杜威击败杜鲁门”的错误头条。后来杜鲁门举着这份报纸的照片，成为政治预测失误的著名典故。
这说明当时很多人看好杜威，但不能把民调领先等同于已经获胜。游戏如果产生杜威胜选，则是模拟的另一种结果，不能拿真实历史的错误头条去证明那个模拟结局也是假消息。

sources.title: 国会图书馆：保存的1948年错误头条及其背景
美国国家档案馆：1948年政治讽刺画与错误头条

notes.title: 以色列：宣布独立、托管终止与美国承认的日期
contains: The Jewish state of Israel is set to declare its independence on May 15, 1948. Will your Administration recognize this new nation?
We will recognize Israel. It is the right thing to do in the aftermath of the Holocaust, and if that's not enough, we can kiss New York good-bye if we don't.
We will not recognize Israel. There's no way we can divert resources from Europe to defend that nation, and we would be seriously jeopardizing our relations with oil-producing Arab states.
The independence of Israel is cause for great celebration among America's Jewish community, particularly in New York.
This certainly hurts you in New York. Perhaps other parts of the country will see things differently.
The Jewish state of Israel is set to declare its independence on May 15, 1948. Do you support Truman's decision to recognize this new nation?
I've supported the Israeli state from the beginning. I'm glad that Truman came around, but he absolutely sent the wrong message by vacillating on this issue until the very last moment.
I support the Israeli state, and I'm pleased that Truman and I are in agreement on this issue.
I believe it was a hasty and impetuous move by the Truman Administration to support the creation of Israel. I have to come out against this measure.
It's good to support Israel, especially if you expect to win your home state this fall.
This seems to be a change of heart from your earlier position.
body: 原问题把宣布独立写为5月15日。杜鲁门图书馆的详细时间线区分：本·古里安在当地5月14日宣读宣言，英国托管于当地5月15日零时终止；美国在华盛顿时间5月14日傍晚给予事实上的承认。时差和不同事件不能混成同一个时间。
正文保留原日期，旁注说明差别。事实承认与法律承认也不同；美国正式的法律承认在1949年。支持承认并不自动等于承诺派美军保卫这个国家。

sources.title: 杜鲁门总统图书馆：宣布、托管终止与承认的详细时间线
美国国家档案馆：承认声明原件与事实／法律承认

notes.title: 《塔夫脱—哈特利法》：否决不等于没有生效
contains:
Congratulations! You have won the 1948 Presidential Election.

In a comeback for the ages, you defeated Thomas Dewey and shocked the nation. Prepare for another four years in the White House. There is much work to be done. You have an ambitious domestic agenda, and face a dangerous foreign situation with the Soviet Union. With a new Democratic majority in Congress, you can hopefully push for universal health care and a repeal of the Taft-Hartley Act.

A wave of strikes and economic turmoil has led to bipartisan support for a new labor law. The Taft-Hartley Act, limiting the power of labor unions, has been placed on your desk. Will you sign this bill or veto it?
Sign it. Labor actions in the steel and coal industries nearly paralyzed our economy, and the public is fed up.
Veto it. This law goes too far, and besides, we won't have a chance without the support of labor.

We have already passed the Taft-Hartley Act and a modernized system of price supports for food, and their effect can clearly be seen in the drop in inflation since 1947. I'm confident this trend will continue.
This might make you look a bit more moderate, but your relations with labor have gone from bad to worse. It is probably not worth it on the balance.
You've redeemed yourself in the eyes of labor and energized the Democratic base.
It's probably best not to praise the effects of Taft-Hartley during this campaign if you want to keep labor happy.
A wave of strikes and economic turmoil has led to bipartisan support for a new labor law. Do you support Truman's decision to veto the Taft-Hartley Act?
Absolutely not. This is a perfectly reasonable measure, designed to prevent a strike in one industry from crippling the American economy.
I support Truman's veto. The National Labor Relations Act was put in place to protect the rights of labor, and it should be respected.

Just in the past 12 months, Congress has passed the Marshall Plan and Taft-Hartley with bipartisan support. They have passed an expansive farm bill, and will be considering housing legislation soon. I don't see why I couldn't work with this Congress.
Nearly every Republican in Congress voted in support of Taft-Hartley, and Robert Taft is a key member of the party. There is definitely consternation at your stance.
body: 这项限制工会权力的法律是在1947年通过的。杜鲁门否决后，国会推翻否决，使其生效。游戏中的“支持否决”和“法律已经通过”，因此并不互相矛盾。
1948年竞选回顾此前的争论，并非同年第一次提出该法。原选项把它列入“过去十二个月”的政绩，是较宽泛的时间概括；距1948年党代会已经超过十二个月。工会是否认为它公平，与联邦政府有没有依法实施它，也是不同问题。

sources.title: 美国参议院：杜鲁门否决与国会推翻否决的记录
美国参议院：罗伯特·塔夫脱与第八十届国会

notes.title: 民权条款、迪克西民主党人与军队种族隔离
contains: A young, liberal Senate candidate from Minnesota named Hubert Humphrey is pushing for a civil rights plank in the Democratic platform. You can either encourage this movement or nip it in the bud.
Our chances are bad enough without instigating a Southern walkout from our convention. This kind of thing will have to wait until our position is a little stronger.
I don't have anything to say on this plank one way or the other. I'm prepared to accept the judgment of my party on this issue.
I support a civil rights plank in the Democratic platform. We can't concede this issue to Republicans and the Progressive Party if we want to compete in the industrial states.
I support a civil rights plank, and furthermore I will personally take executive action to desegregate the Armed Forces. I believe we can turn the black vote if we take initiative on this issue.
You've averted a Thurmond candidacy, but there are also complaints about your vacillation on this issue that could cost you outside of the South.
This is nearly the worst of all worlds. You've come off as indecisive as well as unprincipled, and left a bad taste for many.
Strom Thurmond will cost you some southern states, but hopefully you can make up for it in other regions.
To what extent will you emphasize your support for civil rights legislation in New York as you hit the campaign trail?

Not only will I speak about this issue, but I will use it to attack Truman. I've supported civil rights all along, while Truman seems to have come around at the 11th hour, and for transparent political gain.
I think part of any good campaign involves speaking about my past, and as Governor of New York I successfully pushed for some of the first anti-discrimination laws in the country.
My record speaks for itself. For the time being, we just need to keep the party energized and avoid any statements which might be deemed as controversial.
“Dewey hits back on civil rights” say the headlines. People are noticing.
body: 汉弗莱1948年推动民主党民权条款时，尚是明尼阿波利斯市长和参议员候选人；不是已经在任的联邦参议员。民权争论引发南方种族隔离派的反抗，瑟蒙德成为另一个总统候选人。
杜鲁门7月26日发布第9981号行政命令，确立军队不因种族等因素而区别待遇的政策。实施整合需要时间，并非签字当天所有单位就完成融合。支持党纲、行政命令和争取选票，是相关但不同的行为。

sources.title: 美国参议院：汉弗莱的1948年演说与1949年起的参议员任期
美国国家档案馆：第9981号行政命令原件与执行过程
杜鲁门总统图书馆：1948年左右两翼挑战

notes.title: 柏林封锁：占领区、飞地与空中走廊
contains: The Soviet Union has blocked West Berlin from receiving any supplies from Western Europe. What are your thoughts on this situation?
It's not very practical to defend West Berlin, in its isolated location, if the Soviets continue to escalate. I'd prefer to focus on building our defenses in the rest of West Germany.
We need to do whatever it takes to ensure that Berlin is adequately supplied. We cannot further embolden Soviet aggression by retreating from the agreed-upon boundaries in our 1945 settlement.
The Soviet takeover of West Berlin provides additional ammunition to your Republican critics.
The Berlin Airlift, as it is called, is making headlines in the United States and is definitely helping to restore your popularity.
Do you have any comments to make on the Soviet blockade of Berlin, and the airlift in progress to resupply that city?
I would have us move into East Germany if this blockade continues. We're the ones with a nuclear bomb. Why should we be afraid of the Soviets?
I support our current airlift and hope that it leads to an agreeable conclusion.
We need to pull back from West Berlin and maintain a more realistic defense perimeter. We're more likely to be drawn into World War III than to gain anything useful from the defense of that exclave.
The Berlin Airlift is dominating the headlines and building positive sentiment for Truman. But that's the way things go...
Not only is Truman enjoying a wave of positive publicity for the Berlin Airlift, but your own ideas seem extreme to the public.
This stance has appeal to what remains of the isolationists, but to most it seems like a dangerous retreat in the face of Communist aggression.
body: 西柏林是处于苏联占领区之内、由西方盟国控制的城区。1948年封锁主要切断铁路、公路和水路，空中走廊仍可用于补给，所以不能把原文“任何物资都进不去”理解成不存在空运。
游戏中的“东德”“西德”在这个年份应联系德国东西占领区理解；两个德国国家正式成立是在1949年。苏联接管西柏林的反馈是玩家选择导致的架空分支，不是现实中的柏林空运最终结局。

sources.title: 美国国务院：1948—1949年封锁、空运与德国内部分区

notes.title: 忠诚审查、非美活动委员会与麦卡锡的区别
contains: Do you stand by your decision to implement a loyalty program for employees of the federal government? Do you believe that Communist infiltration is a serious threat right now?
Is the House Un-American Activities Committee going too far in its attempts to root out Communist influence, or should it be doing more?
I support the HUAC, although I do wish it could be a little more aggressive in its rooting out of Communist influence.

I support this program, but I'm concerned with some of the actions I'm seeing from the FBI and the House Un-American Activities Committee. We need to balance this program with appropriate concern for due process and civil liberties.
I'm prepared to go even further on this issue. I will personally oversee a sweeping investigation of the State Department, Department of Defense, and other agencies which are prone to infiltration.
The HUAC is a necessary defender of American values, and I don't see anything to criticize in its current conduct.
The HUAC is not something I plan to address very much as I campaign.
I'm not very comfortable with the activities of this committee, and I believe they should be scaled back to a minimum.
It's a little tone-deaf to speak out so much against the anti-Communism trend at this point.
Of course you've expressed reservations in private, but it's going to be difficult to win this fall if you're defending yourself against Communism allegations everywhere you go.
Anti-Communism is a popular opinion, but you also come off as a flip-flopper and a grandstander with this sudden announcement.
Henry Wallace has instantly derided you for such comments, though they might be playing well in the heartland.
It's probably not best to speak out against anti-Communism movements in public, no matter your personal feelings.
Just lately, it seems like this committee has uncovered shocking revelations about Communists in government. Americans definitely want to see more of this.
To what extent are you prepared to make anti-Communism an issue in this campaign, or to attack Harry Truman on the issue?
Not only is this a serious issue, but Harry Truman is complicit in it. It is no secret that he is, along with most Democrats, complacent on the issue of Communist infiltration.
I think there are legitimate questions to be asked about how much the Communists have embedded themselves into departments of the government. I support the measures we have in place to combat this.
People had their doubts about whether you were prepared to energize your base with the communism issue, but you have proven them wrong.
A number of Congressional candidates have made anti-Communism and accusations of Communist sympathies a centerpiece of their political campaigns. Do you support this trend?
The vitality and way of life in our country is under constant attack from Communism. I support any measure which combats that ideology.

You know, in a few isolated cases, we do have people in this country who are too sympathetic towards Communism to hold public office, in my opinion. But we shouldn't let such accusations get out of hand.
I think this bodes ill for the future of American politics. I support debate on legitimate political issues, but not the casual and spurious accusations about Communist sympathies.
For the most part, Americans support the efforts to reduce Communist influence in this country.
Supporters want to see vigilance on the Communism issue.
body: 1947年第9835号行政命令规定行政部门雇员的忠诚审查程序；众议院非美活动调查委员会则属于国会。联邦调查局、行政机关和众议院委员会不是同一个机构。
原作的反共指控有真实冷战背景，但选项里的指控不自动构成有罪事实。1948年的众议院调查，也不能直接说成由参议员麦卡锡主持；旁注区分机构，保留玩家支持加强审查或保护公民自由的不同立场。

sources.title: 第9835号行政命令全文：行政部门忠诚审查程序（美国总统项目）
美国众议院：1948年阿尔杰·希斯传票与非美活动委员会记录

notes.title: 杜威—史塔森辩论：反共与禁党不是同一立场
contains: If you'll remember my debate with Harold Stassen, I got this nomination in the first place by remaining above such type of politics.
This is somewhat true, but it seems like you are leaving a potential line of attack on the table.
What do you have to say about your announced running mate, Harold Stassen?
Harold Stassen is a great man who represents my views for the future of this country. Now let's get going with this campaign.
body: 两人1948年5月17日在俄勒冈州通过广播辩论，核心问题是是否取缔美国共产党。史塔森赞成取缔，杜威反对用禁党解决问题。
因此，杜威援引这场辩论，并不等于他支持共产主义，也不表示反对一切针对间谍、暴力或颠覆的法律。游戏给出史塔森作为替代搭档，是模拟组合，不是实际共和党票组。

sources.title: 明尼苏达历史学会：1948年5月17日史塔森—杜威广播辩论原稿
美国国会1948年5月18日记录：引用辩论中的现有法律论点

notes.title: 1948年的华莱士与进步党
contains: I support a civil rights plank in the Democratic platform. We can't concede this issue to Republicans and the Progressive Party if we want to compete in the industrial states.

I'm going to eviscerate Henry Wallace and bring the so-called Progressive Party back into the fold. I support universal health care and civil rights just the same as they do, and they are running for vanity's sake alone if they support Wallace.
You're repeating isolationist talking-points and trashing your own policies as President. What is going on?
You're repeating Henry Wallace talking-points and trashing your own policies as President. What is going on?
Henry Wallace has instantly derided you for such comments, though they might be playing well in the heartland.
Not only are you opposing a popular measure, but you're using the leftist rhetoric of Henry Wallace as you do so.
This idea does not appeal to most Americans, though you might get a few Henry Wallace supporters.
body: 这里是富兰克林·罗斯福的前副总统亨利·华莱士，代表1948年的进步党参选；不是1968年的乔治·华莱士，也不能与1912年的罗斯福进步党简单视为同一个组织。
该党支持民权等改革，并批评杜鲁门的冷战政策。游戏中民主党人说对手只是为满足虚荣而参选，是党派攻击；旁注不把这个动机判断当成已证实的史实。

sources.title: 杜鲁门总统图书馆：1948年进步党党纲史料
杜鲁门总统图书馆：亨利·华莱士与1948年竞选

notes.title: 两届惯例、第二十二修正案与麦金莱的情况
contains:
Congratulations! You have won the 1948 Presidential Election.

You have become the first Republican to win the White House in 20 years. You face a dangerous foreign situation, and your domestic agenda is likely to be opposed by Democrats and conservatives alike. Conversely, the support and confidence of the Republican establishment is almost guaranteed. With luck, you might become the first two-term Republican since Ulysses Grant.
What do you think about the proposed Constitutional Amendment to limit the President to two terms in office?
I support this Amendment as a necessary step towards the political health of this nation. We need to, periodically,  have a fresh point of view in government. Ours is not an imperial nation.
I believe strongly in the two-term precedent, but I don't believe it should be enforced by Constitutional Amendment.
I don't have a strong stance on this Amendment. I support the popular will of the people on this issue.
There should not be a limit on how many terms a President can serve. This is why we have an election every four years -- to gauge the will of the American people.
Given the popularity of FDR, it is generally Republicans who favor the two-term limit.
Some die-hard Roosevelt supporters agree, but overall there is broad support for the Amendment.
Most Republicans favor this Amendment after the overreach of FDR. Many wonder why you see things differently.
body: 1948年，总统两届任期限制仍是拟议修宪问题；第二十二修正案在1951年才获批准，而且对当时在任总统有例外。惯例、获选次数和完整任职年数不能混为一谈。
原作杜威胜选结局称可能成为格兰特以来首位two-term共和党总统。如果理解为赢得两次选举，麦金莱在1896和1900年已经做到；如果强调完成两个完整任期，麦金莱则在第二任期遇刺身亡。正文保留原作概括，旁注说明措辞歧义。

sources.title: 美国国家档案馆：第二十二修正案全文及1951年批准日期
美国参议院：麦金莱1900年成功连任
美国国家档案馆：1900年选举结果及麦金莱遇刺日期

notes.title: 联合国核管制：不是已经签成的核裁军条约
contains: Do you advocate the international control of nuclear weapons under the United Nations?

I think this is a necessary expedient which we should implement immediately. It is important to set a precedent now, before other countries develop the bomb, that nuclear war will never again become state policy.
Only if we had clear assurances that other nations would not develop a nuclear bomb, and a means of enforcing those assurances.
We need to be realistic. Would the Soviet Union do such a thing if they developed a nuclear bomb? I would never support this action.
body: 1946年的艾奇逊—利林撒尔报告与巴鲁克计划，提出国际管制原子能、防止核扩散的安排。不同国家对机构权限、核武器处置与实施顺序存在分歧，并没有由此实现统一的国际核管制。
游戏选项讨论无条件支持、先取得其他国家保证或拒绝，是不同的政策判断。不能把“国际管制”直接改写成美国已经单方面销毁全部核弹。

sources.title: 美国国务院：艾奇逊—利林撒尔与巴鲁克计划

notes.title: 杜鲁门主义与马歇尔计划：两种援助背景
contains: In general, what is your view on the providing of foreign aid to American allies?
What are your views, in general, on the Marshall Plan?
We are the only thing standing between the world and global domination by the Soviets. I'm prepared to take any measure to prevent the advance of Communism.

I support this kind of thing in limited cases where there is a clear threat. But I'm worried about some of the ill-defined, open ended commitments we are getting ourselves into with other countries, and with the United Nations.
This is a drain on American finances for a cause that threatens to entangle us in future wars, not of our making. I oppose the actions we have taken.
I support the Marshall Plan and believe that it is a force for the future peace and prosperity of our world.
Obviously, Europe needs some kind of aid after the horrors of World War II. I will be careful to see that this plan is fairly administered and does not become excessive.
The Marshall Plan is a waste of resources, and will slow the development of Europe by forcing nations to rely on foreign subsidies, rather than rebuilding their own economies.
The Marshall Plan is provocative towards the Soviet Union, and is likely to lead to further aggression and escalation from them.
You're repeating isolationist talking-points and trashing your own policies as President. What is going on?
You're repeating Henry Wallace talking-points and trashing your own policies as President. What is going on?
The Marshall Plan is one measure of Truman and George Marshall that has broad support.
What do you have to say about the provision of large-scale military and economic aid to Turkey and Greece, to prevent a Communist takeover in those countries?
I support this aid and think it is a necessary step to combat the Soviet Union.
I support this aid, but I think we could have been more careful about the cost.
I do not support this action that we have taken.
This package was yours from start to finish. You need to stand by it.
body: 杜鲁门主义以1947年援助希腊和土耳其的政策为重要起点，涉及军事与经济援助；马歇尔计划则以欧洲战后经济复兴为核心，1947年提出、1948年立法。
两者与遏制共产主义扩张的冷战战略有关，但不是同一个法案或同一种援助。原作中关于援助会导致依赖、侵略或未来战争的说法，保留为候选人的政治判断，不冒充客观因果定论。

sources.title: 美国国务院：1947年杜鲁门主义
美国国家档案馆：1948年马歇尔计划立法及1947年演说

notes.title: 众议院选总统、参议院选副总统
contains:
No candidate captured an Electoral College majority.

This leaves everyone in a bad situation. Segregationists from the South are demanding concessions before they will support a candidate, leaving the House deadlocked. Perhaps you can work out a deal with Dewey to circumvent this, based on who has the plurality of popular and electoral votes. It's always possible that one of you could serve as the other's Vice President.

No candidate captured an Electoral College majority.

This leaves everyone in a bad situation. Segregationists from the South are demanding concessions before they will support a candidate, leaving the House deadlocked. Perhaps you can work out a deal with Truman to circumvent this, based on who has the plurality of popular and electoral votes. It's always possible that one of you could serve as the other's Vice President.
body: 无人获得过半数选举人票时，宪法规定众议院从总统得票前三名中选总统，州代表团各一票；参议院从副总统得票前两名中选副总统。不是由众议院同时选出一整套搭档。
游戏设想候选人达成交易或一方出任另一方副总统，是政治叙事的简化。协议仍需符合候选范围及各院程序，不能只凭普选领先或两人握手就自动转移职位。

sources.title: 美国国家档案馆：第十二修正案与后续修正案全文

notes.title: 天主教候选人与休斯敦演说
contains: Anti-Catholicism has been a huge issue thus far in the campaign, with hundreds of pamphlets and leaflets being distributed across the South and Midwest. Do you have any comment?

Anti-Catholicism continues to be an issue. Major newspapers have published a statement by 150 Protestant clergy, including Norman Vincent Peale, opposing any Catholic as President. Do you have any comment?
Let's gather some of these leaflets and show them to the media and to major newspapers. I think they demonstrate the lengths that some people will go to discredit my candidacy.
I will attack the idea that any good Protestant would vote against my candidacy because I happen to be a Catholic.
We can't be out there responding to every little two-bit leaflet that some crank puts out. Let's wait and see how this issue develops.
Let's take this opportunity to make a major speech on the topic. I will address this issue exclusively in a televised speech, and put it to rest for good.
Let's put a couple of statements into my next campaign speech to address this issue, and reassure the public that I take no orders from the Pope.
I am Catholic and proud of it. I will not respond to bigoted attacks or innuendo, and I trust that these attacks will only help me by driving higher Catholic turnout.
The impulse is noble, but you come across as a little petty as you awkwardly read from these leaflets at your latest press conference.
You might get away with this for awhile, but be careful that you don't let these attacks snowball.
Giving this speech was a good idea. Many people were impressed, and it provided good material for future advertisements.
This is an acceptable response, but it wouldn't have harmed you to be a little more bold.
It won't cripple your chances of winning the election, but there are some concerns about how passive you've been on addressing this issue.
This will help you drive turnout in the northern states, and hurt a little in the South.
Honestly, I'd rather that people didn't bring this issue up. People know that Kennedy is Catholic, and this can only galvanize his support from that sector.
I wouldn't go to these extremes, but anyone should be concerned about a President who is forced to follow the dictates of the Pope.
Not particularly. Our campaign would prefer to move on to other issues to be perfectly honest.
Again, I'd have to say that this is a valid concern. This would set a dangerous precedent for the independence of our nation's executive.
It's best to stay clear of the Catholicism issue. Anybody who thinks it's important in this election already knows about it.
body: 肯尼迪在1960年9月12日对大休斯敦牧师协会发表演说，明确主张政教分离，总统不接受教会对公共政策的指令。这里的Catholic是天主教，新教牧师与天主教神职人员不能混成一个教派。
游戏里的反天主教指控是当时的竞选偏见或玩家可选攻击，不是证明天主教总统必定服从教宗的事实。原问题关于150名牧师及皮尔的具体说法仍保留；这篇演说本身不能单独证实那个精确人数，也不把所有选项当作肯尼迪真实说过的原话。

sources.title: 肯尼迪总统图书馆：1960年9月12日休斯敦演说全文

notes.title: 金博士被捕：旧交通案、缓刑与慰问电话
contains: Recently, Martin Luther King Jr. was arrested at a sit-in in Atlanta, and has now been sentenced to four months in prison for failing to get a Georgia driver's license after moving to that state. Do you have any comment or action you would like to take?
Let's make a call to Mrs. King to offer our condolences, and let's demand the release of Mr. King.
Let's make a public comment criticizing this arrest, and expressing our hopes that this situation doesn't escalate any further.
I will give a statement encouraging the State of Georgia to protect the safety of Mr. King, while criticizing him for participating in these inflammatory and illegal protests.
This definitely helps you with the black and liberal vote in the north.
You and Kennedy are both making public statements, and it seems like people outside the South are generally upset at King's imprisonment for such a trivial offense.
This seems like an overly critical response where Dr. King is concerned.
body: 1960年10月，金博士参与亚特兰大静坐后被捕。研究所整理的时间线区分静坐指控与此前交通案：静坐指控撤销后，他仍因被认定违反旧案缓刑而转押。不能把这简化成静坐本身获判四个月，或新发现驾照问题后立即入狱。
肯尼迪打电话给科雷塔表达关切，罗伯特·肯尼迪也联系司法官员。这里的condolences按活着的丈夫遭监禁的语境译为慰问，不是丈夫死亡后的哀悼。金博士获释后的采访表示感谢，但仍公开保持不为候选人背书的立场；支持肯尼迪的父亲与金博士本人不能混同。

sources.title: 斯坦福金研究所：基于金的文字整理的亚特兰大被捕章节
斯坦福金研究所：1960年10月27日获释后的采访原稿

notes.title: Quemoy、Matsu、Formosa：金门、马祖与台湾
contains: Do you believe that the islands of Quemoy and Matsu should fall within the United States defense perimeter in Asia?
We need to dispatch an armed garrison to these islands, to make sure there is no mistaking our commitment in our fight against Communism.
I do believe we should defend these islands. We are committed to the defense of Taiwan, and that commitment must include all of Taiwan to be credible.
It wouldn't be responsible of me to comment at this point. As President I will consult with our military leaders to determine what is appropriate.
I'm not sure it's practical or desirable from a military standpoint to defend two tiny islands that are much closer to the Chinese mainland than they are to Formosa.
People want to see a President who is tough on Communism, but even some staunch anti-Communists feel that sending troops to such tiny and remote islands is ill-advised.
This is a good answer for this situation.
Nixon is questioning your hesitation on this issue. Fortunately, however, the average voter has never heard of Quemoy and Matsu.
Kennedy is questioning your hesitation on this issue. Fortunately, however, the average voter has never heard of Quemoy and Matsu.
body: Quemoy与Matsu指金门和马祖，Formosa是当时英语中对台湾的称呼。选项争论离大陆较近的外岛与台湾防卫之间的关系，不能把三者译成同一个地点。
1958年国务院电报区分条约对台湾、澎湖的共同防卫承诺，以及总统判断保卫相关阵地是否有助于台湾、澎湖防卫的权限。保卫台湾并不等于条约已经无条件要求保卫每一座外岛；派驻美军、维持承诺、征询军事意见分别保留。

sources.title: 美国国务院外交文件：1958年9月28日电报及共同防卫范围

notes.title: “导弹差距”：竞选指控与后来情报
contains: Do you believe that current levels of defense spending are adequate?

We have a missile gap, and an overly tight monetary policy that is constraining our growth. I'm very concerned that these shortfalls will allow the Soviet Union to gain an advantage if they are not addressed.
I believe that we need more vigilance in the area of defense, for both military equipment and for missile development. We currently have a missile gap with the Soviet Union.
We can always find areas for improvement, but we have successfully defended the United States and our allies from numerous Communist threats over the past eight years.

In the final analysis, every dollar spent on defense is taken from more productive uses within our economy. I will look for ways to find common ground with the Soviet Union so that we can cut defense spending.
This is a core argument of your campaign, and a good place to differentiate yourself from the Republicans.
Eisenhower is furious that you would join the Democrats in repeating the inaccurate “missile gap” allegation.
This won't hurt you too much, but it does nothing to differentiate you from Nixon and Eisenhower.
This is definitely too soft of a stance to take on the issue of military spending and the Soviet Union.
body: “导弹差距”在这里指美国被认为落后于苏联的战略导弹能力，不是两枚导弹之间的距离。这个说法是冷战焦虑与1960年竞选争论的一部分。
中央情报局对CORONA项目的历史说明指出，1960年8月开始成功回收的卫星影像，随后帮助纠正对苏联导弹及轰炸机实力的高估。正文保留候选人的指控，不把它当作已经验证的军事现状；这些资料也不能单独证明每个候选人在发言时掌握了哪些机密情报。

sources.title: 中央情报局博物馆：CORONA影像与导弹差距评估

notes.title: U-2事件：遗憾、道歉与侦察政策
contains: Should the United States apologize to the Soviet Union for the controversy surrounding the downed U-2 spy plane and surrounding espionage?
We lost a lot of ground diplomatically after this event, and much of that could have been avoided had we issued a formal apology.
A formal apology sounds a bit extreme, but we could certainly have expressed our regrets and perhaps saved the Paris Summit from collapse.
Absolutely not. We cannot show weakness in the face of the Soviet threat, and the Paris Summit collapsed from the intransigence of Nikita Khrushchev.
The headlines today say, “KENNEDY ADVOCATES APOLOGY TO SOVIET UNION”, which is probably not a good thing.
The headlines today say, “NIXON ADVOCATES APOLOGY TO SOVIET UNION”, which is probably not a good thing.
Nixon needles you a bit on this point, but it isn't too controversial.
A few people are interpreting this as a criticism or repudiation of Eisenhower, which does not play well for you.
body: 1960年5月1日，美军情报体系使用的U-2侦察机在苏联领空被击落，飞行员鲍尔斯被捕。美国最初的气象飞行解释遭到证据反驳，随后承认侦察活动。
艾森豪威尔拒绝正式道歉，巴黎峰会最终破裂。表达遗憾、正式道歉、停止特定飞越行动与彻底停止所有间谍活动，是不同承诺。选项对苏联责任的判断是候选人立场，旁注不把所有指责当作客观定论。

sources.title: 美国国务院：U-2飞越、鲍尔斯被捕与巴黎峰会

notes.title: 小石城：执行法院裁决与联邦用兵
contains: Did Dwight Eisenhower do the right thing when he sent federal troops to Little Rock to ensure the integration of the high school there?

There have been a large number of sit-ins recently, where black students and activists are sitting at whites-only lunch counters and department stores to advocate for desegregation. Do you support this movement?
This movement has my full support, as do the other civil rights measures of our day. I will push for a Civil Rights Act as President.
I support the civil rights movement, but I'm a little concerned about the disregard for the law that some of these activists have shown.
These activists are trespassing on the property of lawful businesses. I think there are better methods of pushing for change in the South.
He absolutely did, and I would like to see further action to desegregate our schools and enforce our civil rights.
I believe that Eisenhower did what he had to do in this case, to make sure the decisions of our Supreme Court are enforced.
We should have found a better way to resolve this issue, rather than intrude into the sovereignty of an American state.
This seems like a coded argument for segregation to some.
This seems like a coded argument for segregation to some, and is also a repudiation of Eisenhower.
body: 1957年9月，艾森豪威尔将阿肯色州国民警卫队置于联邦指挥之下，并派遣第101空降师，保护黑人学生进入小石城中央高中，执行取消学校种族隔离的法院裁决。
1960年的问题是在评价此前事件及民权运动。支持法院判决、赞成动用联邦军队、支持静坐与担心擅入私人场所的法律争议，不能合并成一个立场；以州权为种族隔离辩护的选项也保留其政治含义。

sources.title: 美国国家公园管理局：小石城九人与1957年干预时间线

notes.title: 老年医疗：保险方案失败不等于所有援助失败
contains: There was a recent effort in Congress to pass a program to provide medical care to elderly Americans, but it was narrowly defeated. Will you make a further push for this type of program as President?
This program is a good starting point, but I would much prefer a program of national health insurance for all Americans -- not just the elderly.
I would redouble our efforts on this front. Too many of our nation's elderly are unable to afford decent medical care in their advanced years.

I prefer a slightly different program, offering health insurance to the elderly that they can choose to purchase. The proposed program was mandatory, and also covered only those covered by the Social Security Act.
This program would represent a massive new financial commitment for the federal government, when care of the elderly properly rests with the affected family.
This will certainly galvanize your base, but it's hard to imagine that you can get national health insurance passed after the failures of Truman on this front.
National health insurance is not a Republican issue.
This is exactly what your party wants to hear and will push for on this issue.
You are definitely going against the Republican Congress on this issue, but it could work to your benefit.
This is really more of a Republican idea, and it's not like old-age health insurance is unpopular...
This is right in line with the goals of your party.
This is definitely an extreme stance for a Democrat to take.
You're taking a big chance by breaking with Eisenhower and advocating a pretty conservative position on this issue.
body: 社会保障署1960年时间线说明：8月23日，参议院否决肯尼迪—安德森的医疗保险修正案，同时通过经修改的克尔—米尔斯方案；9月签署的法律向州提供符合条件的老年人医疗援助。
因此，原问题的“一项提案被否决”不能扩写为当年没有任何老年医疗法案通过。社会保障筹资的保险、经经济状况审查的援助、自愿保险和全国全民医疗覆盖，都是不同制度；也不能提前把1965年Medicare的最终制度套到每个1960年选项上。

sources.title: 美国社会保障署：1960年保险修正案、克尔—米尔斯方案及立法

notes.title: “工作权法”：不是政府保证人人有工作
contains: What is your position on the power of labor unions in the United States?
Labor unions have been needlessly undermined by the Taft-Hartley Act, and by self-serving investigations from both parties. I will do anything I can as President to support our nation's laborers.
I support unions and I oppose the excesses of leaders such as Jimmy Hoffa. Unions, cleansed of their corrupt elements, should play a central role in the American economy.
We should be vigilant against labor union excesses, and the Taft-Hartley Act was a good start. I believe that we should keep that law in place.
We need to do anything we can to reduce the power of labor unions in this country, including a national right-to-work law.
This is a little incongruous with some of what you and Robert Kennedy have been doing recently in the area of investigating union abuses.
This is absolutely not what you need to say if you want to win this fall.
This is exactly what your party wants to hear.
This seems a little too union-friendly for many potential Republican voters.
You yourself voted against Taft-Hartley, and now you are reversing yourself in the midst of an election? For what reason?
This is way out there for a Democrat. What do you mean by this?
body: 美国劳资争论中的right-to-work，涉及就业能否以加入或支持工会为条件，并不是赋予每个人由政府提供工作的权利。原选项要求全国性法律，比现有州层面的限制更进一步。
《国家劳资关系法》第14(b)节允许州或领地禁止将工会会员资格作为就业条件的协议。限制这类协议并不等于禁止工会或所有集体谈判；废除《塔夫脱—哈特利法》与支持全国工作权法也不是同一方向。

sources.title: 美国国家劳资关系委员会：《国家劳资关系法》第14(b)节

notes.title: 霍法与工会调查：反腐不等于反对所有工人组织
contains: What is your position on the power of labor unions in the United States?
Labor unions have been needlessly undermined by the Taft-Hartley Act, and by self-serving investigations from both parties. I will do anything I can as President to support our nation's laborers.
I support unions and I oppose the excesses of leaders such as Jimmy Hoffa. Unions, cleansed of their corrupt elements, should play a central role in the American economy.
We should be vigilant against labor union excesses, and the Taft-Hartley Act was a good start. I believe that we should keep that law in place.
This is a little incongruous with some of what you and Robert Kennedy have been doing recently in the area of investigating union abuses.
This is absolutely not what you need to say if you want to win this fall.
This is exactly what your party wants to hear.
This seems a little too union-friendly for many potential Republican voters.
body: 这里的霍法是卡车司机工会领导人吉米·霍法。参议院1957年成立调查劳资不当行为的特别委员会，由麦克莱伦主持，罗伯特·肯尼迪担任首席法律顾问，调查工会及劳资领域腐败和犯罪影响。
约翰·肯尼迪、罗伯特·肯尼迪、委员会与工会本身是不同主体。支持调查腐败、赞成劳工组织、限制工会权力、要求霍法下台，是可以分别表态的议题，不把选项简化成所有工会一律犯罪。

sources.title: 美国参议院国土安全与政府事务委员会：调查小组历史及1957年特别委员会

notes.title: 国会党派与未承诺选举人
contains:
No candidate has won a majority in the Electoral College.

The Democrats have an advantage in the House of Representatives, so you are probably in good shape. However, a lot depends on how you deal with Harry Byrd. It's possible that some kind of deal will need to be struck with Byrd or Nixon to get a clean majority in the House.

No candidate has won a majority in the Electoral College.

The Democrats have an advantage in the House of Representatives, so you are probably in bad shape. However, a lot depends on how Kennedy deals with Harry Byrd. It's possible that some kind of deal will need to be struck for any candidate to get a clean majority in the House.
Alabama - Unpledged
This might help you in the Deep South, but it will definitely not help with black and liberal turnout in other regions.
Your words of support help as LBJ begins campaigning in the South. He will cajole and strong-arm that region's politicians into disavowing the unpledged elector movement.
You are definitely going against the Republican Congress on this issue, but it could work to your benefit.
body: 1959—1961年的第86届众议院由民主党占多数，不能把原文Republican Congress误读成当时共和党控制整个国会。医疗方案反馈按上下文译为国会中的共和党人，并在校订记录中披露这一理解。
Unpledged指没有预先承诺支持特定总统候选人的选举人，不是尚未决定投票的普通选民。1960年实际有15张总统选举人票投给哈里·伯德；游戏中的交易是模拟叙事。众议院在无人取得选举人票多数时选总统，按州代表团一州一票，不能仅凭全院某党席位多数就断定结果。

sources.title: 美国众议院史料：第86届党派席位
美国国家档案馆：1960年选举人团计票
美国国家档案馆：第十二修正案

notes.title: “上镜”与1960年电视辩论
contains: After eight years of Dwight Eisenhower, two youthful candidates compete to be his successor. Kennedy is a Senator with a moderate record, a telegenic face, and high-minded rhetoric. Nixon is the sitting Vice President with a strong Cold War record, moderate economic views, and potential likeability problems. Nixon begins the campaign as the slight favorite, but every region of the country could be competitive. Key issues are the Cold War, civil rights, and health care.
Let's be cautious with this idea. Nixon is a skilled debater, and the last thing we need right now is a campaign setback on national television.
I would love to go against Nixon in a televised debate. We could use the exposure and I'm confident that I would win.
Nixon is better known than you are, you're a good debater, and you're telegenic. Why would you not want to debate him?
You've managed to come across as Nixon's equal in these debates, and that alone is a good start...
You are the clear winner in the first debate, and it shows in the sudden enthusiasm of your crowds.
Let's be honest with ourselves. Kennedy is great on television and he did very well debating Hubert Humphrey in the primaries. We should probably avoid this.
I've been a champion debater for my entire life. I'd be happy to go against Kennedy on TV.
Eisenhower advises you to avoid a debate with Kennedy, and you accept that advice. Voters are a little upset that you won't appear, but it could always be worse...
Kennedy has managed to come across as your equal in these debates, and that alone is a good start for him...
Kennedy was the clear winner in the first debate, and it looks like he's received a bump in the polls.
body: telegenic指在电视镜头前形象、表达效果良好，不是拥有电视技术。1960年9月26日的首场总统候选人电视辩论，使两人的镜头表现成为广受关注的竞选因素。
肯尼迪图书馆记述两人的健康、服装、对镜头的表达方式，以及尼克松后来几场的改善。这并不能证明所有观众意见相同，也不能把游戏里“赢下辩论”的反馈理解为正式裁判结果或只凭化妆就决定选举。替代搭档的剧情仍是架空选择。

sources.title: 肯尼迪总统图书馆：1960年竞选与电视辩论

notes.title: 《迪克西》：歌曲与南方政治暗示
contains: This obviously helps in the South, but it hurts you in other areas. Some towns insist on playing Dixie at your campaign events, and other such things...
body: 这里的Dixie是歌曲《迪克西》，不是1948年迪克西民主党人的党名。歌曲有黑脸滑稽歌舞演出背景，后来与南部邦联及南方白人身份产生强烈联系。
乔治梅森大学的史料解读同时指出，它的使用并不只限于南部，林肯也喜欢这支曲子；在民权运动语境中，它会让黑人联想到奴隶制与种族主义。游戏暗示竞选场合播放歌曲有政治信号，不据此断言每个演奏者动机相同，或把所有模拟场景认证为真实行程。

sources.title: 乔治梅森大学History Matters：以史料分析《迪克西》的多重意义

notes.title: 尼克松落选结局：当时的预判与真实后来
contains:
Sorry, you have lost the 1960 Presidential Election.

A lot of people think this election was yours to lose, and party operatives are already whispering that Nelson Rockefeller will be the frontrunner in 1964. As such, it appears that your chances of becoming President are over. Perhaps you can return to California and run for Governor, or for the Senate again.
body: 原作落选结局认为尼克松当总统的机会已经过去，这是剧情在1960年的预判，并非真实历史的最终结论。
尼克松在1962年加利福尼亚州长选举中再次失利，但1968年重新取得共和党提名并赢得总统选举。正文保留原作叙述，不擅自用后来发生的事实改写玩家的模拟结局。

sources.title: 尼克松总统图书馆：1960、1962年的失利与1968年当选

notes.title: 达拉斯抗议与伯德夫人的称呼
contains: Lady Bird Johnson, LBJ's wife, has been spat on by a gathering of far-right protestors in a Dallas hotel lobby. What are your thoughts?
I have no real comment to make, but I'm sure that the voters in Texas will be incensed at the incivility of this episode.
One ugly incident may not swing too many voters to your side, but any little bit helps late in a campaign.
Everything is going well, except for an unfortunate incident in Texas which is giving Lyndon Johnson some good publicity there. Good luck tonight!
body: Lady Bird是克劳迪娅·约翰逊的昵称，译作伯德夫人；不是在讲一种鸟。第六层博物馆保存的1960年11月4日达拉斯竞选照片，记录约翰逊夫妇遭遇支持者与反对者人群，进入阿道弗斯酒店会场。
这份照片及馆藏说明能支持围堵、抗议的背景，不能单独证实原问题“向她吐口水”的具体动作。正文保留原作说法，细节仍需进一步档案核对；“反而获得宣传好处”也是顾问的政治判断，并非照片证明的因果关系。

sources.title: 第六层博物馆：1960年11月4日达拉斯竞选照片及馆藏说明

notes.title: 紧缩货币、整笔拨款与最高边际税率
contains: We have a missile gap, and an overly tight monetary policy that is constraining our growth. I'm very concerned that these shortfalls will allow the Soviet Union to gain an advantage if they are not addressed.
We need to minimize the federal funding of education, even in block grants. It could easily open the door to federal control of our schools.
We need more spending and lower interest rates, and we need to repeal the Taft-Hartley Act and put more money into the hands of the American people.
We must do better. Our present Administration has advocated a hard money policy which caused the recession of 1958 and left idle industrial capacity in our country.
We are on the right track economically. We can't deny that there was a recession in 1958, but the recovery has been strong and 1960 will see a very high rate of growth in this country.
What would you do as President to combat increasing unemployment in America's industrial cities?
Currently the highest income tax bracket pays a rate of 91%. Will you work harder to cut tax rates as President?
I would be open to this, depending on how the economy goes in the next year or two.
We need to cut this rate substantially. It is way too high.
body: hard money在这些降低利率、刺激就业的选项中译为紧缩货币政策，不是字面上的硬币或1844年的金属货币制度。联储历史资料记录1960年衰退及货币政策变化，但候选人把经济问题归咎于艾森豪威尔，是竞选论证，不能据此证明一切责任都在总统。
block grants译为整笔拨款，指为较宽泛用途提供资金并给接受者较大使用裁量，并非街区建设补助。国会研究处的定义用于解释术语，不把后来的具体制度全部套到1960年的提议上。
最高91%的所得税率是边际档税率，不是所有收入都扣掉91%，也不是所有纳税人的实际平均税负。同期国会记录讨论这一最高税档；这里保留原数值，不替玩家计算税务。

sources.title: 联邦储备历史：1951至1960年代中期的货币制度
国会研究处：整笔拨款的定义与受款者裁量
1960年国会记录：最高91%税率的争论

notes.title: 1964年的通胀与失业：原文数值有疑点
contains: If elected as President, what would you do to lower the inflation rate in this country, which currently stands at over 4%?
Our inflation is being caused by all of this Great Society nonsense that Johnson passed. I will slash these programs, slash our deficits, and end our inflation problem overnight.

The inflation rate we have in this country speaks to the heart of the Democrats' problems in running the economy. They claim to be the party of the working man, but they are fine with debasing wages and property values with their misguided social engineering.

Right now we have the strongest economy almost in the history of the United States. Unemployment is at 3% and our national output is growing at a furious pace. Compared to this, our 4% inflation rate is a pretty minor concern.

The Republicans are grasping at straws with this inflation argument. They know that Kennedy and Johnson have managed the economy far better than Eisenhower, so they are resorting to the only argument they have left.

These new federal programs we’re making are only serving to speed our inflation problem. We’re going to cut federal bureaucracy, slash tax rates, and let the private sector pull the people up into the wealth we as Americans are capable of.
There's been a lot of talk from your camp about cutting spending to reduce the growing inflation, what programs would you have in mind?
First and foremost, cuts will be in foreign aid.
For too long, farmers have been stopped from participating properly in the free market. Cutting their subsidies will benefit both the budget and the farmers.
I’m not sure. Maybe everywhere, really.
body: 原作问题写通胀超过4%，一个选项又写失业率3%。总统经济报告的历史统计表显示，1964年CPI-U年度平均涨幅为1.3%，民间失业率年度平均为5.2%；12月同比CPI涨幅为1.0%。这些并不支持原文作为1964年全国通常指标的概括。
译文保留原数字，旁注说明史实差异，没有改动游戏数值或选项效果。年度平均、单月值、不同物价指数必须区分；将通胀完全归咎于某个候选人的政策，仍是选项中的政治论证，不是统计表直接证明的因果关系。

sources.title: 总统经济报告：表B-64，消费者价格指数变化（数据来源BLS）
总统经济报告：表B-43，民间失业率（数据来源BLS）

notes.title: 伟大社会与Medicare：承诺、倡导与实施的区别
contains: Your 'Great Society' has been a major part of your campaign promises, but many potential voters are wondering how you plan to come through on some of these promises- like slashing poverty. Would you care to expand on your plans?
Let’s talk about the Great Society, the Civil Rights Act, and my accomplishments in office.
We’re going to expand welfare, expand Social Security, expand Medicare, and give the average American a leg up. It’s what the American people deserve.
We’re seeing a lot of growth with what we’re doing now, and the last thing we should do is rock the boat. You won’t see any big changes to government policy in my next term.

These new federal programs we’re making are only serving to speed our inflation problem. We’re going to cut federal bureaucracy, slash tax rates, and let the private sector pull the people up into the wealth we as Americans are capable of.

Let's focus on the Great Society- Medicare, Social Security expansions, and the Civil Rights Act. These are all things I have championed in my first two years, and I will champion them further in my next four.
Let's give them a real show- promise expansions to Civil Rights, more Social Security and welfare expansions, and a continued commitment to liberal ideals.
body: 伟大社会是约翰逊的改革议程，涉及减贫、教育、医疗等领域；并不是所有项目在1964年竞选时就已经立法或实施。Medicare的1965年法律于7月30日签署，主要制度在1966年开始运行。
原选项中“扩大Medicare”的说法保留，但此时应联系尚在争取通过的老年医疗保险方案理解。福利、社会保障现金给付、老年医疗保险也不是同一种项目。原文“执政头两年”另有时间概括问题：约翰逊在1963年11月继任，至1964年大选尚不到一年，不能按两个完整任职年理解。

sources.title: 美国国家档案馆：1965年Medicare与Medicaid法律
美国社会保障署：签署与筹备运行的历史
美国国务院人物资料：肯尼迪任期至1963年

notes.title: 学校祷告案：官方组织与个人信仰
contains: Would you appoint federal judges who support the decision Engel v. Vitale outlawing mandatory school prayer?
This decision was atrocious. I don't think it's an exaggeration to say that our way of life is at stake here when we don't allow our schools to teach basic moral values to our children.
I was disappointed with this decision. I would certainly appoint judges who see the wisdom in teaching our kids a few lessons about morality.

We have Catholics, Jews, and others in this country who should not be forced to pray in a certain way because of what some principal believes in a public school. This is a First Amendment issue in my opinion.
I will appoint judges who support religious freedom in the United States. Absolutely.
body: 1962年恩格尔诉维塔莱案涉及纽约公立学校采用官方制定的祷文。最高法院认为，政府组织的这种宗教活动违反第一修正案的政教分离原则，即便祷文声称不属于某一教派、学生可以不参加，也不能消除问题。
原问题以“强制学校祷告”简写，不能扩写成法院禁止孩子所有私人祈祷、禁止信仰或禁止一切道德教育。选项中关于道德沦丧或宗教自由的说法，分别是候选人立场。

sources.title: 美国联邦法院教育资料：恩格尔诉维塔莱案事实与理由
美国判例汇编原件：370 U.S. 421

notes.title: 赫鲁晓夫下台：党领导人与总理分由两人接任
contains: Nikita Khrushchev, Premier of the Soviet Union, has been overthrown by Leonid Brezhnev! This has hurt the Goldwater campaign, which has been using belligerent quotes from Khrushchev to gather votes from foreign policy minded voters.
He can’t stop shooting himself in the foot!
If he keeps talking like that, we won’t even need to campaign.
body: 1964年10月，赫鲁晓夫被迫下台。勃列日涅夫接任苏共中央第一书记；柯西金接任部长会议主席，即总理。不能把党领导人与政府总理合并成勃列日涅夫一个职位。
原问题用勃列日涅夫概括这次权力更替，正文保留其叙事，旁注说明两人的职务。勃列日涅夫的称号在1966年才改为总书记；“这损害戈德华特竞选”的说法是游戏判断，不是当时国务院文件证明的选票测量。

sources.title: 美国国务院：1964年10月17日评估赫鲁晓夫更替的备忘录
美国国务院：勃列日涅夫、赫鲁晓夫与柯西金的职务时间

notes.title: 《抉择的时刻》：里根为戈德华特助选
contains: Famous actor Ronald Reagan has given a long speech in support of Barry Goldwater in California. The speech, immediately popular nationwide, has been dubbed ‘A Time For Choosing.’
You’d think he’d have retired from politics by now.
He should stick to movies if he has any sense.
body: 里根1964年10月27日的电视演说，后来通常以《抉择的时刻》闻名，支持戈德华特，阐述减小政府、个人自由、强硬反共和自由与集权对立的政治主张。此时他是演员和政治演说者，还不是总统。
这些是演说者的立场，不是译者认定所有数据与指控都正确。游戏里“他该继续拍电影”的话，是对跨入政治领域的嘲讽，并非对后来里根政治生涯的历史结论。

sources.title: 里根总统图书馆：1964年10月27日演说全文

notes.title: 博比·贝克：国会调查不等于刑事审判
contains: A new wave of Goldwater’s attack ads have gone out across the nation, highlighting Johnson’s involvement with Bobby Baker and Bill Sol Estes!

Goldwater’s campaign continues to hit your campaign hard on the Bobby Baker and Billie Sol Estes scandals, accusing you of being a corrupt, lying cheat! What actions, if any, should we take to downplay the issue?

I will not deny that I knew and worked with Baker and Sol Estes back in the 50’s- that is public knowledge. However, not once did I take part in nor know of either of their fraudulent schemes. I trust that my name will be exonerated as the truth comes out.

These are desperate, slanderous attacks from the Goldwater camp. I hardly knew either of these two men when I was in office, and I trust that the legal system will handle this situation with competence and tact.
We should be talking less about Bobby Baker and Billy Sol Estes and more about my great successes in office.
Those damn conmen!
Despite your best efforts, the Bobby Baker trial remains as an ugly mark for Goldwater to needle you on.

Bobby Baker was a protege and good friend of yours, and your business connections with both men in the 50’s have been widely publicized. Your numbers take a big hit as both Goldwater and the press rakes you for this outright lie. Best hope this blows over soon...
Your openness surprises many analysts, but perhaps the impact of the scandal is lessened by your honesty? It’s hard to say.
A new wave of attack ads have gone out across the nation, highlighting Johnson’s involvement with Bobby Baker and Bill Sol Estes.
Johnson’s weak point is the Bobby Baker case. Let’s talk about Baker and Billy Sol Estes.
This is a weak point of Johnson’s, and is sure to hurt him..
body: 博比·贝克曾担任参议院多数党秘书，1963年辞职后受到调查。参议院规则与行政委员会在1963至1964年举行听证，调查利益冲突与财务不当行为。
原反馈在1964年说“贝克审判”，正文保留，但国会听证不是法院刑事审判；参议院后来的调查史料把贝克的法院审判记在1967年。贝克、埃斯蒂斯与约翰逊的关联被用作竞选攻击，也不能只凭关联就推定总统本人参与了每项欺诈。游戏中对某个回答“撒谎”的评价是顾问反馈，旁注不扩写为独立司法定罪。

sources.title: 美国参议院：1964年贝克案调查及听证日期
美国参议院情报调查史料：贝克审判1967年开始

notes.title: 《一个共和党人的自白》：竞选广告的角色发言
contains: Moderate Republicans have been quite dissatisfied with the course of Goldwater’s campaign, and many major figures on the liberal-moderate wing have refused to endorse him. There may be an opportunity to win these moderates over. Should we go for it?
How could we pass up an opportunity like this? I want the ad men on this, as soon as possible.
It’s no use. Those men haven’t voted for a Democrat since Roosevelt. Let’s keep focusing on the groups we know we can win.
'Confessions Of A Republican', as it’s called, is making waves across the North in moderate Republican circles.
body: 这是约翰逊阵营1964年的电视广告，画面中的共和党选民角色表达对戈德华特的担忧，并表示宁愿投民主党候选人。广告用跨党派选民的叙述争取温和派，不是司法意义的认罪自白。
广告原件与对白保存在影像博物馆的竞选广告档案中，影像来自约翰逊图书馆。游戏说它在北方“引起轰动”，是效果反馈，不能把一则广告推定为所有共和党选民的真实意见。

sources.title: 影像博物馆Living Room Candidate：1964年广告原件与对白

notes.title: 三K党背书与候选人立场：不是会员身份的同义词
contains: Another story has broken our way- Goldwater has received an endorsement from the leader of the Alabama Ku Klux Klan!

Though it may seem like a foregone conclusion to attack Goldwater on the Klan endorsement fiasco, the fact remains that we are still behind in the South, where the Klan still has substantial influence. Should we press this line of attack?
Are you kidding? What we’ll lose in the South, we’ll make up ten times over in the rest of the country. Run the ads.
Making up ground in the South is better than expanding our massive lead in the North. It hurts me to say it, but hold back on the attacks for now.
Goldwater has received an endorsement from the leader of the Alabama Ku Klux Klan. LBJ has already capitalized with attack ads going out nationwide. What should we do?

Having recently received endorsements from the Ku Klux Klan and the John Birch Society, you need to find a way to distance yourself from extremists and put yourself into the American political mainstream.
I want to remain silent on this.
These groups have a right to free speech, but Goldwater is neither a Klan member nor a Bircher.
We need to reject this endorsement right away.
I hate to admit it, but we need whatever support we can get. Keep quiet on this.
The Klan’s endorsement is bad enough for your reputation. Your silence on it is worse.
body: 阿拉巴马州三K党领导人支持戈德华特，成为1964年竞选攻击的重要素材。但某个极端团体的支持，并不自动证明候选人是该团体成员；是否谴责、是否接受支持、是否赞同其主张也是不同问题。
国家档案馆依据竞选史料讨论了戈德华特、米勒及团队对种族议题和背书的不同反应。选项可选择拒绝、沉默或辩护，保留其政治区别；顾问预测南方或北方选票得失，不当作所有当地选民态度一致的证明。

sources.title: 美国国家档案馆Prologue：1964年白人反弹、背书与候选人的反应
影像博物馆：1964年三K党背书攻击广告原件

notes.title: 1964年民权法：民权、州权与执行现行法律
contains: Despite your best efforts, there’s no question about it- there’s a massive divide between the Northern, integrationist wing and the Southern, segregationist wing of the Democratic Party. Do you have a plan on bringing the two back together- at the least, for this election?

Civil rights continue to be a major issue of the times, with African-American activists like MLK and Malcolm X still marching on the streets for further enforcement and expansion of the Civil Rights Act. What should be our campaign’s approach to them?

Hubert Humphrey is one of the most outspoken liberals in the Democratic Party, and that reputation seems to be following him- Goldwater has recently denounced him as a 'left-extremist'. Should we step in to defend him?

They have a point. The Civil Rights Act was watered down by obstruction and interference from segregationist senators, and I’d like to see one with better protections make it to my desk in my second term.
We’ll be sure to enforce the Act to the best of our abilities. Anything past that, I can’t. We’ll do what we need to do, whether that’s another Act or not.
Haven’t we done enough? The Civil Rights Act of 1964 was enough of a pain to pass. We’ve given them what they want- I can’t make any promises on legislation past that.

I am the candidate of stability, of safety, and of responsibility. Civil rights will be treated with the care and attention it requires under a Johnson Presidency, with no extreme actions for one side or the other.
I am the candidate of hope and change. In my next term, I will advance civil rights even further, and create a society that is equal in every way. On this, I give my word.

I am the candidate of responsibility and pragmatism. Civil rights has been advanced as far as it must be- any further action will simply be federal overreach, and must be avoided. The South has nothing to fear from a Johnson Presidency.
Your civil rights position is the most controversial part of your campaign. Would you like to clarify your position to help ease the fears of Southern Democrats or Northern moderates?
Let it be known that I side with the states on the civil rights issue. I will not change this.

I would like to clarify in regards to the Civil Rights Act of 1964. Despite my vote against the bill, I will uphold it as President. I would like to see it repealed- I still believe it is unconstitutional- but a President cannot ignore laws that he dislikes.

I would like to change my previous position. With the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, I shall make no attempt to remove this law, but I will oppose further legislation, such as mass busing or forced integration.
I would like to remind civil rights conscious voters that I was fighting for civil rights long before they were popular, as well as helping found the Arizona Chapter of the NAACP.
Want to know who's at fault for this Civil Rights Act? It's Hubert Horatio Humphrey.

We'll need to pivot left somewhat if we want to cut in on Johnson's majority. By promising to respect the Civil Rights Act and highlighting our own forwardness on the issue, we can assuage liberal fears.
This clarification helps downplay your radical reputation, while also dampening damage done to your numbers among those who are voting for your civil rights positions.

This is a big shift from your earlier stance. While it may improve your standing with Midwestern moderates, those who were voting for you because of your civil rights position are quite upset and demoralized.
This attack will do little to help win anybody but outspoken segregationists.
Your last second switch on civil rights appeals to moderates as much as it angers Southern voters. Will they sweep you to victory?
body: 1964年《民权法案》针对公共设施、就业等领域的歧视，并扩展联邦执行权。它不等于当年已经通过1965年《投票权法》，也不能概括成一签字便解决所有种族隔离与投票障碍。
反对某项法律、希望国会废除它、承诺总统依法执行它，是可以并存的立场。州权在这些段落里与种族隔离争论相联系，保留其政治含义；跨区校车接送则是学校融合手段，不是普通公共交通。原选项关于创建NAACP州分会的具体个人功绩仍需专门档案核对，本条法案来源不证明该个人传记细节。

sources.title: 美国国家档案馆：1964年《民权法案》原件与各项保障
美国参议院：结束民权法案冗长辩论

notes.title: 南方重组与“边界州”：原文地理概括
contains:
America in 1964 stands unsettled, memories of the beloved late John F. Kennedy still prominent in the nation's memory. As the nation recovers from the shock of November 1963, the 1964 campaign is just beginning, with questions swirling around America’s course in Vietnam, Social Security, and Civil Rights, among others.
  • Lyndon B. Johnson aims to maintain his large lead in the polls, defending his policies while keeping both integrationist and segregationist voters of the Democratic Party on board.
  • Barry Goldwater hopes to make up ground quickly, reuniting his party behind his conservative vision after a contentious primary, as well as flipping the South for the first time since Reconstruction.

Despite your best efforts, there’s no question about it- there’s a massive divide between the Northern, integrationist wing and the Southern, segregationist wing of the Democratic Party. Do you have a plan on bringing the two back together- at the least, for this election?
Why should I tie myself to the sinking ship that is the Southern Democrats? With the numbers I have, they should be begging me for help. Either get with the program, or get the hell out of my way.
Let’s talk about Southern issues and our commitment to respecting the rights of the states.
The Deep South has been Goldwater's stronghold this whole election, but they're Democrats at heart. We'll swing through Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia to wrap this up.
We need to double-down on the states rights issue. Our only hope of victory is through the South.
Let’s campaign in the border states- Arkansas, Tennessee, and North Carolina.
This appeals to Southern voters, with the downside of driving moderate Northern voters away.
You have made a final appeal to Southern voters, at the expense of moderate support elsewhere. Will it be enough to win?
body: 原背景说自重建以来首次让南方转向共和党，若理解为任何南方州首次投共和党，则不准确：1928年胡佛已赢得德克萨斯、佛罗里达、弗吉尼亚等南方州。戈德华特在深南部的突破，与整个南方同时转党不是一回事。
原选项把阿肯色、田纳西和北卡罗来纳称为border states，保留这个称呼，但它们不是内战中留在联邦的典型蓄奴边界州；那些通常指特拉华、马里兰、肯塔基、密苏里及后来成立的西弗吉尼亚。这里应理解为竞选路线的较宽泛地域说法，不擅自改州名单或访问效果。

sources.title: 美国国家档案馆：1928年各州选举结果
美国国家公园管理局：内战边界州的构成与历史

notes.title: 结局的夸张、杜威典故与连任资格
contains:
Congratulations! You’ve won the 1964 Election!

It comes as no surprise to anyone but the most devoted Goldwater supporters, but you have emerged victorious from the 1964 Election- an outcome that was never in doubt. Your supporters sit back in smug satisfaction as Goldwater delivers a muted concession speech, and you can rest assured that another four years in office awaits you.

Who knows what the future holds? If all goes well, maybe you can run again in 1968. Make sure to keep the economy chugging and the Vietnam War going smoothly, or you may be in trouble- Goldwater seems to have kicked the hornet’s nest of conservatives, and they’ll be looking to challenge you in the future...

Astounding! You have lost the 1964 Election!

In an utterly flabbergasting turn of events, the Democratic landslide forecast by every pundit from May to November has been turned completely on its head. They may be struggling to explain it on ABC, but the news is true all the same- by a combination of the Goldwater campaign’s competence, your complete and utter collapse in the last few months, and what seems like divine intervention, Barry Goldwater will be the next President.

There’s a lot of blame being thrown around the Democratic Party, and almost all of it is directed at you. To blow such a commanding polling lead is almost unheard of- indeed, some whisper that you intentionally sabotaged your campaign, as ridiculous as this may be. No matter the reason, your political career is over. Best read up on Thomas Dewey.

A tie has been forced in the 1964 Election.

How did this manage to happen? America stands surprised at the unexpected outcome before them- for the first time in over a century, a winner has not been decided on Election Night. By some strange miracle, Goldwater has battled his way back just far enough to tie the election.

You have nothing to fear about losing the Presidency, of course- Democrats control both the Senate and the House- but already, questions are being raised about your viability as a candidate. After all, if someone as unpopular as Goldwater could catch up to your lead, imagine what a Nixon could do? Best pray your ideas are as successful as you hope.

Amazing! You’ve defeated the odds and won the 1964 Election!

They said a miracle would be needed for Barry Goldwater to win, and it seems a miracle has taken place. Your supporters flood the streets as pollsters and pundits struggle to explain how this occurred. By shrewd competence, good fortune, and what seems like divine intervention, Barry Goldwater has won the election.

Where you go from here is anyone’s guess. Undoubtedly, your effectiveness will be decided by the makeup of Congress- it will certainly be yet another struggle to pass your agenda through the moderates and liberals that make up much of the government- but for now, sit back and relax, knowing you’ve pulled off an upset greater than 1948!

You have forced a tie in the 1964 Election.

America stands surprised at the peculiar situation before them- for the first time in over a century, the winner of the Presidency has not been decided on Election Night. Through some combination of a furious comeback on your behalf and a cruel joke played by God, you have neither failed to or defeated Lyndon Johnson for the Presidency- an exact tie has occurred.

As impressive as this feat is, the cruelty of the situation doesn’t end there- Democrats control both the Senate and the House, all but dooming your chances at winning. At the least, take pride in the conservative revolution you have brought to Congress- and, if you’re still open for it, perhaps your old seat in the Senate will be open sooner or later.
body: “最好读读杜威的经历”借1948年民调看好杜威却最终败选的逆转，讽刺玩家丢掉巨大优势；不是说1964年真实历史也发生了戈德华特获胜。1948年真实败者与模拟胜者分别看待。
原作“一个多世纪以来首次选举夜没有胜者”是夸张概括，1876年海斯与蒂尔登的争议就拖到次年。平局时众议院选总统按州代表团投票，参议院另选副总统，不能只用全院党派席位推出必然结果。
第二十二修正案规定，为他人任期代任超过两年者只能再获选一次。约翰逊1963年11月继任至1965年1月不足两年，故1964年当选后仍可争取1968年提名；原作胜利结局不需要为此修改游戏规则。

notes.title: 陈香梅事件：秘密联络与游戏分支
contains: Sources have indicated that Johnson is close to reaching a breakthrough in negotiations with the North Vietnamese, which could almost assure a Democratic win on Tuesday. An operative with connections to the South Vietnam government is willing to sabotage these negotiations with promises that you will offer a better deal when elected. Will you take a chance on this plan?
I refuse to condone this kind of a plan. I have limits on what I will do to win an election.
This will guarantee victory for us if successful. Let's roll the dice.
As word of a possible peace deal breaks, Humphrey is surging in the final polls. Will you have the votes you need on election day? Sit down and watch the results come in.

The peace talks collapsed on the final weekend before the election. Unfortunately, the news has also broken that you had something to do with it! Settle in to watch the returns, and pray that you can somehow pull this out...

Your gamble has paid off. Humphrey's momentum was halted when the peace talks collapsed, and there hasn't been a word in the news to suggest you had a part in it. The only thing left to do now is to watch the returns come in.

On the weekend before the election, Lyndon Johnson's peace negotiations have collapsed with the North Vietnamese. Even worse, there are rumors that a Nixon operative has sabotaged the negotiations. Nixon swears to you on his honor that he is innocent. Will you make this an issue over the last two days of the campaign?
We have no idea if Nixon was involved in this or not. I won't cheapen the outcome of this election and risk my own reputation with flimsy innuendo.
This is bordering on treason. The American people deserve to hear about this.

You have taken the high road on this key issue, but it doesn't change the fact that peace talks have stalled. Sit down and watch the returns, and pray that you've done enough to pull out what would be an amazing comeback.
The election closes in chaos. Peace talks collapse, you accuse Nixon, Nixon accuses the Democrats of bugging his plane, and the upshot is mass confusion and anger among the voters. Good luck tonight!
As word gets around that Nixon probably sabotaged the Vietnam peace negotiations, you are the clear beneficiary of an 11th hour surge in the polls. Will it be enough to hand you a victory tonight?
The election closes in chaos. Peace talks collapse, you accuse Nixon, Nixon accuses the Democrats of bugging his plane, and the upshot is mass confusion and anger among the voters. Good luck tonight!
It looks like Humphrey has enjoyed a last minute surge in the polls, thanks to a breakthrough in peace negotiations. Will this help cause a deadlock in the electoral college?
body: 约翰逊1968年10月31日宣布停止轰炸北越，推动和平谈判。约翰逊图书馆说明，尼克松竞选阵营中的一些人与南越政府秘密联络，劝其延缓谈判，并暗示尼克松当选后会提供更好的条件；重要中间人陈香梅是陈纳德的遗孀。
约翰逊把这件事称为叛国，但未在大选前公开相关情报，尼克松否认参与。政治上的叛国指责不等于法院已经定罪。游戏允许玩家选择是否参与、是否公开指控，并给出不同成败结果；这些分支及票数变化不是已经发生的历史。不能把南越政府自身的考虑全部简化为美国竞选阵营的指令。

Diplomatic History：越南方面的动机与既有解释的局限

notes.title: 1968辩论是架空选择，1964比较另有疑点
contains: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your performance in debates and campaigning were widely praised compared to 1960, which allowed you to win with a massive landslide. What a turnaround from 1964!
We can't have the American people saying that I'm afraid to debate Hubert Humphrey. Let's do it.
I won't risk a debate with Humphrey. We can defeat him without one.
Unfortunately, Humphrey absolutely trounced you in the debate you agreed to have. Your gamble did not pay off.
Observers agreed that Humphrey seemed to be the better debater, but you avoided any serious mistakes. Overall the impact will be minor.
Wow! You held Humphrey to a draw and seemed in command of yourself throughout. What a turnaround from 1960.
Humphrey will spend the rest of the campaign needling you on this issue. Of course, you've started out with such a lead that it hopefully won't matter in the end.
Richard Nixon, perhaps remembering the debacle of 1960, has expressed little interest in a debate this election. Will you challenge him to one?
The debates in 1960 were an anomaly. If Nixon has no interest this time, I'm fine with that.
This is a real opening for us. I will challenge Nixon on this issue relentlessly.
Why would you not want to debate Nixon? He has an awkward, sometimes surly personality and you would surely look good in comparison.
Nixon refuses to debate you, and most of the voters know it. This will definitely hurt him at the polls.
After cajoling Nixon into a debate, you have absolutely trounced him. This could be a real turning point in your campaign, which started out looking so hopeless.
Nixon agreed to debate you, but unfortunately he did not repeat his 1960 missteps. The inconclusive outcome does little to change the overall picture of the campaign.
body: 真实历史中，1960年肯尼迪与尼克松辩论后，1964、1968和1972年均未举行主要总统候选人之间的大选辩论。游戏允许尼克松与汉弗莱辩论，是玩家可改变历史的分支，胜负评价也属于模拟。
原结局另写“与1964年相比”的翻身。1964年共和党总统候选人是戈德华特，不能把这句话当成尼克松1964年参选或参加辩论的证据。正文保留原比较年份，旁注指出其含混之处，不改分支条件。
